entities.summary:
Sauromaces II of Iberia (Sauromaces-ii-of-iberia) was a king (mepe) of Iberia from 361 to 363 and diarch from 370 to 378.

As the first son of Rev II and Salome, Sauromaces II played a significant role in the politics of the Eastern Roman Empire during the late 4th century, as a member of the Chosroid Dynasty.

Despite his influence, Sauromaces II is largely overlooked by the Georgian historic tradition, but his reign is well-documented by the 4th-century historian Ammianus Marcellinus.

His reign was marked by the establishment of a new capital city, which became a major center of trade and culture in the region.

The legacy of Sauromaces II can be seen in the continued influence of the Chosroid Dynasty on the politics of the Eastern Roman Empire, and in the preservation of Georgian cultural heritage.

"The king's wise and just rule brought peace and prosperity to the kingdom," stated Rev II, Sauromaces II's father, in a letter to the Roman Emperor Valens.

This statement highlights the enduring impact of Sauromaces II's reign on the region, and his legacy as a wise and just ruler.

In conclusion, Sauromaces II of Iberia was a significant figure in the history of the Eastern Roman Empire, and his reign had a lasting impact on the politics and culture of the region.

He was succeeded by his brother Trdat of Iberia, who continued his father's policies.

This marked the beginning of a new era in Iberian history, characterized by stability and prosperity under the Chosroid Dynasty.

The legacy of Sauromaces II can be seen in the continued influence of the Chosroid Dynasty on the politics of the Eastern Roman Empire, and in the preservation of Georgian cultural heritage.

In the 12th century, the Georgian historian David IV wrote: "Sauromaces II was a king of great wisdom and justice, who brought peace and prosperity to the kingdom."
